title: Savanna & Grassland Animals
keyIdea: A grassland is a wide open habitat of grass with few trees. The African savanna has lions, zebras, wildebeest, elephants, giraffes and cheetahs. The American prairie has bison and prairie dogs. Zebras and wildebeest live in big herds because many eyes spot a predator sooner. Lions are predators and zebras are their prey: grass → zebra → lion.
familyTip: Watch a short wildlife clip of the savanna together. Pause it and ask: which animals are predators, and which are prey? Why might the zebras stay close together? Then ask where a small animal could hide if there are almost no trees.

visual.caption: Does each grassland animal eat plants or other animals? Drag each card, or tap it then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort savanna and prairie animals, grow a zebra herd to spot a lion, build grass → zebra → lion, hide a prairie dog, and remove the lions.

kid: A grassland is a wide open place covered in grass, with only a few trees. In Africa it is called the savanna. In North America it is called the prairie.
Lions, zebras, wildebeest, elephants, giraffes and cheetahs live on the savanna. Bison and prairie dogs live on the prairie.
Zebras and wildebeest eat grass, so they are herbivores. They live in big herds. With so many eyes and ears, one of them spots a lion sooner, and the herd runs. That is safety in numbers.

A lion is a predator. It hunts other animals. A zebra is its prey. In the food chain grass → zebra → lion, each arrow points to the eater. There are few trees to hide in, so prairie dogs dig burrows. They dive down when a hawk flies over.
adult: Ages 7 to 9. In the National Curriculum in England, Year 2 living things and their habitats asks children to see that animals live in habitats that suit them and get food from plants and other animals, using a simple food chain. Year 4 adds building and reading food chains with the words producer, predator and prey.

Savanna is tropical grassland with scattered trees and wet and dry seasons. Prairie is temperate grassland in North America. Open ground gives little cover, so many grazers live in herds. More animals watching means a stalking predator is noticed sooner, and each animal's own risk is diluted. Prairie dogs live in colonies, give alarm calls and shelter in burrows. Cheetahs rely on speed in the open, while lions often hunt as a group.

Common mistakes: picturing the savanna as a jungle. Thinking an animal is safer alone because it is harder to see. Reading the food-chain arrow the wrong way round; it points to the eater. Putting bison or prairie dogs in Africa. Thinking that removing predators helps the grass, when more grazers usually eat more of it.

In the lab your child sorts eight animals onto the savanna or the prairie. They grow a zebra herd from 1 to 20 and drag a lion closer to see the bigger herd spot it sooner. They tap grass, zebra and lion into a food chain. They drag a prairie dog into its burrow when a hawk appears. Last, they remove the lions in a simple model and watch zebra numbers climb and the grass disappear.

practice.prompt: Which sentence best describes a savanna?
choices: wide open grassland with a few trees
a thick jungle full of tall trees
a cold desert of ice and snow
practice.hint: Think of where zebras and lions can see a long way across the grass.
practice.explain: A savanna is wide open grassland with only a few scattered trees. A jungle (rainforest) has thick trees, and ice deserts are found near the poles.

practice.prompt: Why do zebras live in big herds on the open savanna?
choices: many eyes and ears spot predators sooner
a herd is harder for lions to see
zebras cannot find grass on their own
practice.hint: Think about what happens when one zebra notices a lion creeping up.
practice.explain: With many zebras watching, one spots the lion sooner and the whole herd runs. A big herd is easy to see; the safety comes from more lookouts.

practice.prompt: On the savanna you see {a} zebras, {b} lions and {c} wildebeest. How many of these animals are prey that eat grass?
practice.hint: Zebras and wildebeest eat grass and are hunted. Lions are the predators.
practice.explain: Zebras and wildebeest are grass-eating prey: {a} + {c} = {=a+c}. The {b} lions are predators.

practice.prompt: A herd has {a} zebras. Each zebra has 2 eyes. How many eyes are watching for lions?
practice.hint: Each zebra adds 2 more eyes. Double the number of zebras.
practice.explain: {a} zebras × 2 eyes = {=2*a} eyes. A bigger herd has more lookouts, so a lion is spotted sooner.

practice.prompt: In the food chain grass → zebra → lion, what does the arrow from zebra to lion mean?
choices: the zebra is eaten by the lion
the zebra runs towards the lion
practice.hint: The arrow points to the eater. Food passes along the arrow.
practice.explain: The arrow points to the animal that does the eating. The lion eats the zebra, so food passes from the zebra to the lion.

pool.prompt: Which animal lives on the American prairie?
pool.hint: The prairie is the grassland of North America.
pool.explain: Bison graze on the North American prairie. Zebras and giraffes live on the African savanna.

pool.prompt: In grass → zebra → lion, which is the predator?
pool.hint: A predator hunts and eats other animals.
pool.explain: The lion hunts the zebra, so the lion is the predator and the zebra is its prey. The grass is the producer.

pool.prompt: A wildlife park shows {a} bison, {b} prairie dogs and {c} giraffes. How many of these animals live on the American prairie?
pool.hint: Bison and prairie dogs are prairie animals. Giraffes live on the African savanna.
pool.explain: Bison and prairie dogs: {a} + {b} = {=a+b}. The {c} giraffes come from the African savanna.

pool.prompt: You count {a} lions, {b} cheetahs and {c} zebras. How many of these animals are predators?
pool.hint: Predators hunt other animals. Zebras eat grass.
pool.explain: Lions and cheetahs are predators: {a} + {b} = {=a+b}. The {c} zebras are prey.

pool.prompt: A hawk flies over the prairie. How does a prairie dog stay safe?
choices: it dives into its burrow under the ground
it stands still in the open grass
pool.hint: There are very few trees on a grassland. Where else can it go?
pool.explain: Grasslands have few trees, so prairie dogs dig burrows and dive underground when danger comes.

pool.prompt: If all the lions left a savanna, what would most likely happen?
choices: zebra numbers would grow and they would eat more grass
the grass would grow much taller
pool.hint: Lions keep zebra numbers down. What happens to the grass if there are more zebras?
pool.explain: Without predators, more zebras survive. More zebras eat more grass. Predators and prey help keep each other in balance.

pool.prompt: A zebra eats only grass. Which word describes it?
pool.hint: Herb- words are about plants. Carni- words are about meat.
pool.explain: A zebra eats plants, so it is a herbivore. A carnivore eats animals. A producer, like grass, makes its own food.

pool.prompt: Which animal is not found on the African savanna?
pool.hint: One of these lives in North America.
pool.explain: Prairie dogs live on the North American prairie. Wildebeest and cheetahs live on the African savanna.
